mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact the S&P 500, leading to higher forward returns.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 20-day horizon more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate exceeds 5% but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates combined with low unemployment indicate tight monetary policy, negatively impacting equity returns.
failure_condition: If the specified conditions are met but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts during economic expansion indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer price inflation may lead to higher interest rates, negatively impacting equity valuations.
failure_condition: If inflation rises but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 100 indicates a supply contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If industrial production is below 100 but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Employment growth without corresponding retail sales growth indicates weak consumer spending, leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: If employment grows but retail sales fall yet S&P 500 returns are positive more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rates stimulate economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If federal funds rates are low but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.
